subtopic: StableHLO / Operator set stability and framework/compiler portability
learningObjective: Explain the design goal of StableHLO as a portable operator set between frameworks and compilers.
stem: Which statement best describes the design purpose of StableHLO?

options.text: StableHLO is a hardware-independent runtime that directly executes ML models on GPU/TPU/CPU without invoking any downstream compiler; it replaces XLA at the execution layer.

StableHLO is a versioned operator set with a formal specification that acts as a portability contract between ML frameworks (as producers) and compilers (as consumers), providing forward/backward compatibility guarantees so framework upgrades and compiler upgrades can proceed independently.
StableHLO is a Python DSL for defining new ops in JAX; it is not an IR and cannot be serialized to disk.
StableHLO is a strict subset of TensorFlow's SavedModel format; every StableHLO program is directly a SavedModel and vice versa.

explanation: StableHLO is the OpenXLA project's versioned, specified operator set designed to serve as a stable interchange format between framework frontends (PyTorch/JAX/TensorFlow) and compiler backends (XLA, IREE, etc.). It has a formal spec, an MLIR dialect, and versioning with forward/backward compatibility guarantees. The goal is to decouple framework release cycles from compiler release cycles.

optionExplanations.A: Wrong: StableHLO is a spec/IR, not a runtime.
optionExplanations.B: Correct: portability contract with versioning and compatibility guarantees.
optionExplanations.C: Wrong: it is an MLIR dialect and a serializable IR, not a Python DSL.
optionExplanations.D: Wrong: StableHLO is not equivalent to SavedModel.

assumptions: OpenXLA StableHLO project design as documented at openxla.org/stablehlo.
nonImplications: Does not imply StableHLO covers every op; the operator set is intentionally scoped.
Does not imply StableHLO removes the need for a compiler; consumers still lower it.

distractorRationales.C: Confuses IR with a Python DSL.
